answers.core: I don't think it's possible for an addon to add a built-in property to another node.
answers.workaround:
## Workaround 1
This can be worked around partially, but unrealistic and it gets annoying real fast. And it works on playing the scene only, not in the editor.
```
func _ready():
	queue_free()
```
## Workaround 2
1. Add 1 OmniLight3D at the middle of the model.
2. Set the light_size to 100m.
3. Set the light_specular to 0
4. Set the light_energy lower if needed.
5. Set the editor_only to true

Not the perfect solution, but it's better than nothing.

## Workaround 3 (Best)

1. Put this script in your WorldEnvironment. It's fully dynamic except for the root scene's name part.
2. You will need to put the name in the **excluded_node_name_list** if your map's name is other than **map** or **world**.

```
@tool
extends WorldEnvironment

var excluded_node_name_list = [
	"map", "world", "node3d"
]


func _ready() -> void:
	if Engine.is_editor_hint():
		var scene_name = get_tree().get_edited_scene_root().get_name()
		scene_name = str(scene_name).to_upper()
		
		for excluded_name in excluded_node_name_list:
			excluded_name = excluded_name.to_upper()
			
			if scene_name == excluded_name:
				queue_free()
	else:
		queue_free()
```

title: Make editor_only property available to the WorldEnvironment
